strengths: Addresses practical problem of long-form VSR with significant efficiency gains (58× speedup) and constant memory usage
Well-designed dual-timescale temporal modeling combining rolling KV-cache (local coherence) and joint visual guidance (global coherence)
Thoughtful training strategy with patch-wise pixel supervision and cross-chunk distribution matching balancing fidelity, consistency, and memory efficiency
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple metrics (fidelity, perceptual quality, pixel-level and semantic-level consistency), extensive ablations, and 7 baseline comparisons
Valuable contributions: MovieLQ benchmark for 1000-frame long-form VSR and adoption of semantic-level consistency metrics (VBench) for evaluation
Strong empirical results achieving top-1 or top-2 performance across diverse datasets and metrics; linear runtime scaling and constant memory enable practical deployment
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured methodology
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (KV-cache, DMD, patch-wise supervision) are from prior work; contribution is primarily in their combination rather than novel algorithms

Heavy dependence on pretrained Wan 2.1 (1.3B) model makes it difficult to assess whether quality gains derive from the method or the powerful prior; no analysis of robustness to different T2V backbones
Marginal quality improvements over strong baselines: PSNR differences often <1dB compared to SeedVR2; main advantage is efficiency rather than quality, which is underemphasized in framing

Training-inference distribution mismatch under-explored: models trained on short sequences (~33 frames) generalize to 1000 frames without theoretical justification or analysis of potential degradation with further length increases
Trade-offs not well discussed: Table 4e shows DMD reduces PSNR (25.04→24.86) while improving perceptual metrics; unclear if trade-off is justified without deeper analysis
Evaluation fairness concerns: 'progressive patch aggregation' applied to baselines for MovieLQ may not be optimal strategy; makes direct comparison difficult and may underestimate achievable quality
Limited generalization analysis: all experiments use ×4 upscaling only; no evaluation on other scales (2×, 8×) or different video types; no failure case analysis

Reproducibility concerns: code link unavailable at review time; method depends on non-public Wan 2.1 model; some implementation details unclear (exact DiT modifications, reference frame selection strategy)
Incomplete technical justification: why (3,3) chunk/cache size is optimal lacks theoretical explanation; reference frame selection (middle frame 'e.g.') not specified; sensitivity analysis absent
Missing analysis: no computational cost breakdown, limited memory usage details beyond peak, no timing profiling of components, insufficient investigation of streaming artifacts at chunk boundaries

strengths: Novel AR-OSD formulation specifically designed for streaming VSR with dual-timescale conditioning (KV-cache + joint guidance) for maintaining temporal coherence
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets with strong results: state-of-the-art quality on UDM10/MovieLQ, 58× speedup over MGLD-VSR, effective temporal consistency preservation
Valuable MovieLQ benchmark contribution addressing gap for evaluating true long-form VSR (1000-frame sequences with real-world degradations)
Technically sound methodology with detailed mathematical formulation, clear architecture design, comprehensive ablation studies, and reproducibility through promised code release
Honest treatment of limitations including computational constraints, training scale restrictions, and dependence on pretrained priors; transparent discussion of future improvements
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for why AR-OSD specifically optimizes temporal consistency; connection between autoregressive formulation and coherence is empirically validated but lacks principled explanation
Critical dependence on pretrained T2V diffusion priors; improvements may partially reflect prior quality rather than proposed methodology; limited ablation on sensitivity to prior strength

Temporal consistency improvements often modest in magnitude (e.g., VBench SC 0.9578 vs 0.9456); error accumulation over very long sequences (>1000 frames) not thoroughly analyzed despite claims about avoiding degradation
Limited algorithmic novelty—individual components (DIT, VAE, distribution matching) from existing work; contribution primarily in system design/engineering rather than new techniques

MovieLQ benchmark limited to ~10 single-shot 1000-frame videos; small validation set for drawing strong generalization conclusions; streaming capability evaluated mainly on fixed sequences rather than true streaming scenarios

Design choices lack clear justification: optimal KV-cache length M=3 shown in ablation (Table 7) but not explained in main text; cross-chunk distribution matching loss motivation unclear; loss weight ratios unexplained
Concurrent streaming methods (FlashVSR, Stream-DiffVSR) relegated to appendix; main comparisons against mostly non-streaming baselines, reducing evaluation comprehensiveness
